content.text: Starbase is a collection of CLI framework crates: lifecycle, events, diagnostics, tracing, terminal output, shell and archive utilities. Michi already has a deliberately narrower split between pure response rendering and pipeline execution, so I’m checking the few patterns that might transfer without expanding its scope.

**The main lesson from Starbase is how to keep a framework modular while giving applications a coherent path from execution to output.** Starbase separates its app lifecycle, events, diagnostics, tracing, and console reporting into crates. Michi has made a similar boundary choice for different reasons: `michi-core` renders agent responses, while `michi-pipeline` executes steps. Starbase supports that direction; it does not make a case for turning michi into a general CLI framework. [Starbase README](https://github.com/moonrepo/starbase/blob/master/README.md), [michi principles](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/PRINCIPLES.md)

| --- | --- |
| A session has explicit startup, analyze, execute, and shutdown phases; shutdown runs after phase failures. [App guide](https://github.com/moonrepo/starbase/tree/master/crates/app) | If `michi-cli` gets a real consumer, define cleanup and failure behavior explicitly. This belongs in that CLI crate, not `michi-core`. |

[Events documentation](https://docs.rs/crate/starbase_events/0.7.3) | Michi’s existing `StepObserver` and `DurableObserver` are a better fit for recording execution. Mutable events would make replay and outcome records harder to reason about. [Pipeline API](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-pipeline/src/exec.rs:45) |
| Console output goes through a reporter layer with buffered stdout and stderr. [Console documentation](https://docs.rs/crate/starbase_console/0.6.14) | A future CLI integration should test that agent output stays parseable when progress and diagnostics are emitted. Michi already has `AgentResponse::render_for()` for choosing the audience. [Response API](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:258) |
| Starbase integrates `miette` and tracing at the application boundary. [App guide](https://github.com/moonrepo/starbase/tree/master/crates/app) | Keep michi’s optional `miette` support and caller chosen logging. The default rendering crate need not own global diagnostic or tracing setup. [Scope](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/docs/spec/05-scope-and-quality.md:38) |

**Recommended next step:** make a small consumer example that uses Starbase for a CLI lifecycle and michi for agent facing results, then inspect the actual stdout, stderr, error, and cancellation behavior. That would test the boundary with real output before proposing another michi primitive. My confidence is high in the architectural comparison, but the value of a new API remains unproven until an independent tool needs it.

content.text:
I surveyed seven GitHub repositories against michi’s actual boundaries: agent output, MCP results, graph validation, pipeline execution, and a possible future CLI. **The strongest immediate finding is a protocol version decision.** Michi’s MCP implementation correctly targets its declared 2025-11-25 spec, but the [2026-07-28 MCP spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools) is now stable and changes the result shape. Michi’s [MCP spec note](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md:1) still calls that release an unshipped candidate.

### How I weighed the repositories

Stars indicate interest, not users or architecture quality. I gave more weight to a clear API boundary, documented tradeoffs, tests of observable output, and evidence of use by another substantial project. Star counts below are approximate GitHub counts checked on October 24, 2026.

| Repository | Adoption evidence | Architectural lesson for michi |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep) | ~69.4k stars; [VS Code uses it for workspace search](https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode/wiki/Search-Issues). | Its reusable search and printing crates sit behind CLI glue. Its maintainer distinguishes convenient human output from the [stable JSON output needed for reliable integration](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/discussions/3404). Preserve that distinction between michi’s compact text and `structuredContent`. |
| [clap](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap) | ~16.8k stars; [uv depends on it](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/Cargo.toml). | A builder provides the core API; derive support is optional. If `michi-cli` gets a real consumer, integrate a CLI parser instead of putting parsing into `michi-core`. [clap source and feature layout](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/main/src/lib.rs) |
| [Tower](https://github.com/tower-rs/tower) | ~4.3k stars; [Axum builds on its middleware model](https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/blob/main/axum/src/docs/middleware.md). | Small `Service` and `Layer` interfaces support optional timeout, retry, and capacity behavior. Tower’s [retry policy](https://docs.rs/tower/latest/tower/retry/trait.Policy.html) asks whether a request can be cloned; michi’s effect and replay model asks the stronger question of whether repeating it is safe. Keep that safety model. |
| [petgraph](https://github.com/petgraph/petgraph) | ~4k stars; dependencies include [rust-analyzer](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/blob/master/Cargo.toml) and [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/Cargo.toml). | Multiple graph representations and algorithms serve broad needs. Michi’s dependency free, deterministic `GraphBuilder → Graph → Dag` serves a narrower contract. Petgraph is a useful comparison oracle for graph properties, not an evident replacement. |
| [miette](https://github.com/zkat/miette) | ~2.6k stars; used by [Starbase’s app framework](https://github.com/moonrepo/starbase/tree/master/crates/app). | Keep semantic error facts separate from their presentation. Its diagnostic code, help, causes, and optional fancy renderer reinforce michi’s existing typed `DomainError` plus opt-in `miette` design. |
| [official MCP Rust SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk) | ~4k stars; an official protocol implementation rather than a proven user count. | Its version handling and [separate transport features](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk/blob/main/crates/rmcp/README.md) make it the best interoperability target for michi’s MCP result assembly. |
| [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) | ~91.1k stars; a large end user tool. | Its [contributor guide](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) tests actual command output with snapshots and uses nextest. Michi already uses those tools; the next useful coverage is a consuming CLI or MCP server test, where rendering, errors, and protocol assembly meet. |

### Findings ranked for michi

**1. Decide and test MCP version compatibility. High priority, high confidence.** The [2025-11-25 spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools) requires `structuredContent` to be a JSON object, matching [michi’s parser and wire schema](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-core/src/mcp.rs:74). The stable [2026-07-28 spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools) permits any JSON value and shows a `resultType: "complete"` protocol result. Michi currently rejects arrays and scalars, including a list result that the new spec permits. That is **not a defect against michi’s declared target**. The actionable work is to update the stale version note, decide which revisions michi promises to support, and test its output through an actual SDK for each promised revision. The consuming server may own the new protocol wrapper; it should not be added blindly to the old inner result type.

**2. Prove the text and structured surfaces together. High priority, high confidence.** Ripgrep’s experience shows why compact display text and machine data should each have a stated contract. Michi already assembles both in [`AgentResponse::to_call_tool_result()`](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:273). A small integration fixture should check that a successful result, a tool error, and a truncated list remain consistent across text, JSON, and `isError`. This tests behavior a consumer sees without adding another primitive.

**3. Keep the narrow graph and pipeline APIs. High confidence.** Petgraph and Tower succeed through general abstractions because they serve many kinds of graphs and services. Michi has different promises: deterministic dependency reports and effect aware resume. Its [graph contract](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/docs/spec/09-graph.md) and [pipeline observer and durable start APIs](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-pipeline/src/exec.rs:45) already express those promises. Importing a general graph representation or middleware stack would need a demonstrated consumer problem.

**4. Make one real integration example the adoption test. Medium confidence.** A small `clap` CLI or `rmcp` server using michi would reveal API friction that unit tests cannot: where output goes, how errors are surfaced, and whether the published types compose easily. This is more informative than adding API based on the popularity of another repository.

One adoption constraint is outside code architecture: [`michi-core` and `michi-pipeline` use FSL-1.1-MIT](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/Cargo.toml:8), while several comparison libraries use permissive licenses; `michi-graph` is MIT. Whether that affects prospective consumers is **an inference to validate with them**, not something stars can answer.

**Recommendation:** address the MCP version note and run a versioned interoperability test first. Then use one independent consumer integration to decide whether michi needs any further API. The research supports michi’s current crate boundaries more strongly than it supports adding new primitives.

Yes. Repositories built for agent tools are more useful comparisons for michi than general Rust libraries. I looked at their tool result contracts and error handling, using GitHub stars as a measure of interest rather than a count of users.

| Repository | GitHub stars* | What michi can learn |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| [FastMCP](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp) | 28.2k | Its `ToolResult` separates readable content, structured data, and metadata. It is the closest comparison for michi’s MCP result surface, although it also owns tool registration and transport. [Tool docs](https://gofastmcp.com/servers/tools) |
| [Deep Agents](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents) | 30.6k | Large results are stored outside the model context, leaving a preview and a way to read more. This supports michi’s explicit truncation signals; storing and retrieving the full result belongs to the host. [Implementation](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/main/libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware/filesystem.py) |
| [Pydantic AI](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai) | 20.8k | Its MCP client distinguishes an error the **model can correct**, a completed failed call, and an exception for application code. Those are different outcomes that adapters must preserve. [MCP client docs](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/mcp/client.md) |
| [Vercel AI SDK](https://github.com/vercel/ai) | 27.5k | `toModelOutput` converts a tool’s returned value into what the model receives. That is a strong precedent for michi’s focus on the presentation boundary. [Tool docs](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/content/docs/03-ai-sdk-core/15-tools-and-tool-calling.mdx) |
| [LangChain](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain) | 148.4k | Tools can return readable `content` alongside a richer `artifact`. Its MCP adapter puts `structuredContent` in the artifact rather than automatically showing it to the model. [Tool API](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/core/langchain_core/tools/base.py), [MCP adapter docs](https://github.com/langchain-ai/docs/blob/main/src/oss/langchain/mcp/tools.mdx) |
| [Airbyte Agent SDK](https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-agent-sdk) | 136 | Smaller, but unusually relevant: it translates connector failures into framework-specific signals and guards output size across several agent frameworks. Technical fit matters more than its star count here. [README](https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-agent-sdk/blob/main/README.md) |

\*Approximate counts shown by GitHub on October 24, 2026. They do not establish production usage or architectural quality.

**The most important finding is that the same MCP result can reach models differently.** LangChain keeps structured content as an artifact. OpenAI Agents Python uses text by default, but can be configured to prefer non-error `structuredContent` over the text blocks. Michi currently emits both a rendered text block and JSON in `AgentResponse::to_call_tool_result()`; its compact text therefore needs a real consumer check, not just a wire-format test. [LangChain behavior](https://github.com/langchain-ai/docs/blob/main/src/oss/langchain/mcp/tools.mdx), [OpenAI Agents behavior and default](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/mcp/server.py), [michi implementation](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:271).

I would prioritize three follow-ups:

1. **Run one michi MCP result through LangChain, Pydantic AI, and OpenAI Agents.** Record exactly what the model sees for success, truncated output, and error. That will show whether michi’s hints and compact rendering survive each adapter.
2. **Document `retryable` precisely for integrators.** In michi it means the *same operation* can be tried again without repeating an effect; a Pydantic AI model retry can instead mean “change the arguments.” An adapter should not equate those two signals. [michi error contract](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-core/src/error.rs:142), [Pydantic AI behavior](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/mcp/client.md).
3. **Keep large-result storage outside core.** Michi can report what was omitted and give retrieval guidance when a host provides a handle. Deep Agents and [Pydantic AI Harness](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/tool-output-limits/) show why the host must own the store, paging tool, and lifetime of that handle. This fits [michi’s rendering boundary](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/PRINCIPLES.md:45).

My read is that michi has a distinct place **between tool execution and agent consumption**. These popular libraries provide tools, servers, and agent loops; several still need application code to decide how a result should be summarized, bounded, and explained. The strongest next evidence for michi is a small set of working integrations showing that its output improves those existing stacks.

content.text:
I examined Cloudflare’s [Agents](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents), [Code Mode](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/tree/main/packages/codemode), [Computer](https://github.com/cloudflare/computer), and [MCP](https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp) code and architecture docs against michi’s current crates. The main lesson is that **“agentic tooling” is several distinct jobs**. Cloudflare has separate pieces for a durable agent, a workspace and its tools, code execution, and tool delivery over MCP. Michi already has useful boundaries of its own; the opportunity is to make those boundaries easier to use together.

| Cloudflare project | Responsibility | Closest michi boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Agents SDK](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/packages/agents/AGENTS.md) | Agent identity, state, scheduling, sessions, and recovery | Mostly host application; some overlap with `michi-pipeline` |
| [Code Mode](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/docs/codemode/runtime.md) | Let a model call tools through generated code, with replay and approvals | A possible caller of michi, not a core primitive |
| [Computer](https://github.com/cloudflare/computer/blob/main/docs/09_tool_interface.md) | Persistent workspace, execution backends, and file tools | A tool provider whose results michi could render |
| [MCP](https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/main/AGENTS.md) | Expose a large API to agents while managing context and protocol compatibility | Closest to `michi-core::mcp` and response rendering |

### What the codebases teach us

**1. Keep the complete execution record separate from what the model sees.** Code Mode’s tool execution returns an audit trail of connector calls, but its `toModelOutput` projection removes that trail and bounds sandbox logs before giving the result to the model. The durable call log remains available for replay. This is a particularly strong pattern: an audit record, a resumable record, and a model response have different requirements. Truncating the replay record would risk changing what resumed code observes. [Code Mode implementation](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/packages/codemode/src/proxy-tool.ts), [runtime design](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/docs/codemode/runtime.md).

For michi, [the pipeline’s `RunRecord`](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-pipeline/src/lib.rs) should remain the execution record, while `michi-core` can render a bounded account of it for an agent. This supports the existing separation between execution and presentation. A concrete example that renders a pipeline outcome for a model while retaining the full record for the host would make the distinction visible to users.

**2. Define tool behavior once, then adapt it to each agent library.** Computer has one tool vocabulary and common limits for AI SDK, pi, and TanStack AI. Its `defineExec` core is independent of those libraries; each adapter changes the host-facing shape. Optional entry points keep one agent library from becoming everyone’s dependency. [Computer tool interface](https://github.com/cloudflare/computer/blob/main/docs/09_tool_interface.md).

Cloudflare has recently reinforced this boundary in its own stack: Think moved its built-in workspace tools to Computer’s `createAITools` and deprecated its older execute-tool API in favor of Computer’s `exec`. So older Think examples are a moving target; the architectural signal is the consolidation around a single tool implementation. [Agents release notes](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/releases).

For michi, I would first build **small integration examples or thin adapters** around the existing rendering and MCP APIs, rather than add framework types to `michi-core`. An AI SDK example and an MCP server example would test whether the same result semantics survive both paths.

**3. Put context limits at the boundary that knows what may be discarded.** Cloudflare uses different strategies in different places. Computer’s file tools return bounded reads and continuation offsets, so a caller can request more. Cloudflare MCP compresses its enormous API catalog into search and code execution tools; in that mode it bounds returned text and marks truncation. Its direct-tool mode has different defaults. Code Mode can let generated code select a small answer before any result reaches the model. [Computer tool interface](https://github.com/cloudflare/computer/blob/main/docs/09_tool_interface.md), [MCP architecture](https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [MCP truncation code](https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/main/src/truncate.ts).

That supports michi’s decision in [PRINCIPLES.md](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/PRINCIPLES.md) to report truncation without deciding which domain items survive. A file tool can paginate; a search tool can rank; a caller can choose survivors; michi can consistently render the result and the fact that content was omitted. Cloudflare’s structural JSON shrinking is useful for its own gateway, but it is not a universal selection policy for michi to copy.

**4. Durable workflows require an explicit account of uncertain side effects.** Cloudflare’s Think action ledger writes a pending action before an effect, settles it afterward, and uses an idempotency key to recover safely. It can pause a turn for approval. A stale pending action without a safe key is surfaced as uncertain rather than blindly repeated. Code Mode has a different recovery mechanism: replay prior connector results, then continue after approval; the code’s call order and arguments must remain consistent. [Think actions](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/docs/think/actions.md), [Code Mode runtime](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/docs/codemode/runtime.md).

Michi-pipeline is already closer to this than a simple DAG runner: it distinguishes whether an effect was applied or is unknown, supports prechecked replay, exposes stable step keys, and makes persistence the caller’s responsibility. Cloudflare’s strongest lesson here is probably an **end-to-end durable-run example**: persist through `StepObserver`, simulate interruption after an external effect, then resume using downstream idempotency. That would show the practical guarantee and its limit. Neither design can promise exactly-once external effects without cooperation from the external system.

**5. Protocol compatibility deserves more attention than another orchestration primitive.** Cloudflare MCP handles client-specific authorization behavior at the server edge and tests real MCP requests. Its experimental generated tools advertise output schemas only to compatible protocol clients and can return a full parsed value in `structuredContent` alongside text. That path is explicitly experimental, but it shows careful protocol versioning and a distinction between structured data and model-facing text. [MCP implementation notes](https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [client handling](https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/main/src/clients.ts).

This exposes the clearest gap in michi’s current surface. [Michi’s MCP spec](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md) targets 2025-11-25, and [its MCP content model](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-core/src/mcp.rs) is text-centered with object-shaped structured content. The published [2026-07-28 MCP tools specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools) allows broader JSON values for structured content. I would review the target-version policy and test the actual serialized wire result against both protocol generations before extending the public API. Cloudflare’s experimental rollout is a useful example of how to stage that change.

### What I would do for michi, in order

1. **Review MCP version compatibility and wire behavior.** Decide which versions michi promises, cover text and structured results with protocol-level fixtures, and make any version-dependent behavior explicit.
2. **Publish one complete integration example.** Take a real tool result through `michi-core` into an MCP client, showing what the model receives and what the host retains.
3. **Publish a durable pipeline example.** Exercise interruption, an uncertain external effect, persistence, and resume with a stable idempotency key.
4. **Use those examples to judge adapter demand.** If multiple users repeat the same AI SDK or MCP glue, extract a thin adapter while keeping michi’s pure rendering and pipeline types independent.
5. **Defer a general agent loop or Code Mode runtime.** Those require sandboxing, approvals, durable storage, and host-specific execution policy. Cloudflare’s code demonstrates the size of that commitment; michi’s current libraries can be valuable to those runtimes without owning one.

The strongest transferable design principle is **one semantic result, several projections**: full data for the host and recovery, a bounded presentation for the model, and a protocol-correct representation for each client. That fits michi’s existing architecture and gives a concrete way to improve it.
Can we think through and validate all of these things before we propose changes?

Yes. I’ll treat the earlier list as hypotheses and check each one against michi’s code, Cloudflare’s implementation, and the relevant protocol requirements. I’ll report which ideas hold up, which are already covered, and which need more evidence before any change is proposed.

Here is the Starbase assessment after checking its published API and michi’s code:

| Starbase pattern | What the evidence shows | Fit for michi |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Application lifecycle | Its `AppSession` runs startup, analysis, execution, and shutdown; shutdown also runs after an earlier phase fails. The latest published API returns an `AppRunOutcome` with the last phase, error, and exit code. [Starbase 0.13.3 docs](https://docs.rs/crate/starbase/0.13.3) | Useful for an application *using* michi. It does not reveal a missing lifecycle primitive in `michi-core`. |
| Separate crates by purpose | Starbase separates its app framework, events, shell, styles, and utilities. [Repository layout](https://github.com/moonrepo/starbase/tree/master/crates) | Supports michi’s existing separation of rendering, graph logic, and async execution; it does not by itself justify another crate. |
| Mutable events | `starbase_events` runs subscribers in sequence and lets them alter event data or stop propagation. [Event crate docs](https://docs.rs/crate/starbase_events/0.7.7) | A deliberate application extension mechanism. Michi’s [step observers](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-pipeline/src/exec.rs:49) serve a narrower progress and persistence purpose. I see no evidence yet that michi needs an event bus. |
| Errors and instrumentation | Starbase lets sessions choose an error type and offers terminal diagnostics and tracing. [Starbase docs](https://docs.rs/crate/starbase/0.13.3) | Michi already has an optional `miette` feature and an explicit [pipeline run record](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-pipeline/src/record.rs:228). A CLI could combine the libraries without making Starbase a dependency of michi. |

Two corrections matter for the broader validation. First, michi’s pipeline already records outcomes, root causes, and steps needing verification, so Starbase’s `AppRunOutcome` is corroboration of a good pattern rather than a gap to fill. Second, the Starbase GitHub code pages available through the browser appear older than its published 0.13.3 docs. I would use a pinned release for any further code-level comparison rather than infer current behavior from those cached pages.

I’m also revising my earlier MCP assessment: michi’s object-only `structuredContent` matches the **2025-11-25 version it claims to support**. The current [2026-07-28 specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools) permits other JSON values and changes more of the result shape. That establishes a version difference, not yet a reason to change michi’s API.

So the validated Starbase lesson is about **clear ownership and preserving execution outcomes**. Michi already applies much of it. Before proposing anything, the remaining test is whether real michi consumers encounter repeated friction that its current boundaries cannot handle. Stars and architectural similarity alone cannot establish that need.

Yes. Looking across Starbase and Cloudflare, several lessons stand out beyond individual features:

1. **The useful abstraction is often an outcome value.** Starbase’s `AppRunOutcome` retains the phase, error, and exit code; Cloudflare retains execution and call records for recovery. Michi already follows this with [RunRecord](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-pipeline/src/record.rs:228), including uncertain outcomes. The lesson is to preserve facts about what happened before rendering them for a CLI, model, or protocol client. [Starbase docs](https://docs.rs/crate/starbase/latest), [Code Mode runtime](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/docs/codemode/runtime.md).

2. **Recovery state must stay close to the effects it describes.** Cloudflare’s durable agent and workspace own storage because they own execution. Michi lets the host persist step records through [DurableObserver](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-pipeline/src/exec.rs:72). Both are coherent choices. A storage backend in michi would need evidence that independent consumers want the *same* persistence behavior, not just evidence that durable runs matter. [Think actions](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/docs/think/actions.md).

3. **Large outputs are sometimes better handled by references than by better truncation.** Computer offers bounded reads and continuation; Code Mode rejects oversized replay values and points callers toward workspace storage because shortening a replay value would corrupt recovery. That reinforces michi’s split between a caller choosing or storing data and michi reporting what was presented. [Computer tool interface](https://github.com/cloudflare/computer/blob/main/docs/09_tool_interface.md), [Code Mode runtime](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/docs/codemode/runtime.md).

4. **A shared semantic contract matters more than a shared framework.** Computer keeps tool names, schemas, and limits consistent across three agent-library adapters. Starbase stays CLI-library agnostic. For michi, this suggests judging integrations by whether they preserve response meaning across Rust, Node, and MCP—not by how many framework adapters exist. [Computer tool interface](https://github.com/cloudflare/computer/blob/main/docs/09_tool_interface.md), [Starbase overview](https://github.com/moonrepo/starbase).

5. **Source popularity is weak evidence of a missing primitive.** Stars show interest. Cloudflare’s MCP design solves a roughly 2,500-endpoint catalog problem; Starbase solves application lifecycle needs. Neither establishes that typical michi consumers need code execution, an event bus, or tool discovery. Michi’s [inclusion checklist](/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/PRINCIPLES.md) asks the better question: are independent real tools repeatedly implementing the same pattern?

6. **Versioned wire contracts need their own validation.** The newer MCP specification changes the tool result shape, while michi deliberately targets 2025-11-25. The next useful evidence is a client and wire compatibility study, including what clients actually show the model. A newer spec alone is insufficient grounds for an API redesign. [2025-11-25 tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools), [2026-07-28 tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools).

My overall assessment is that these repos **validate michi’s existing boundaries more than they reveal a missing major component**. The open questions are empirical: which integrations are being repeated by consumers, where model-visible output loses information, and whether current MCP clients need the newer result forms. Those are worth checking before proposing changes.

I’ll audit michi’s current APIs and examples against the patterns we validated from Starbase and Cloudflare, then turn the findings into a scoped proposal. Yes, but they apply at different layers. After comparing Michi’s code with the four projects, I would **validate consumer integrations before adding another Michi primitive**. The strongest immediate opportunity is Monokl; the strongest reason to change Michi itself is a real need for multiple independently named sections in one agent response.

## What each project tells us

| Project | Verified fit | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Monokl** | Direct consumer. It pins an [older Michi Git revision](</Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/Cargo.toml:71>) and has a [newline workaround](</Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs:12>) for a defect fixed in current `michi-core`. | Make a migration spike the first consumer trial. Compare exact TOON, JSON, errors, and hints before removing the workaround. Keep search ranking and budget decisions in Monokl. |
| **Caliper** | Its canonical `ExtractionOutput` is lossless; its [TOON output](</Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md:88>) is an intentionally lossy agent projection. That matches the useful separation in Cloudflare’s tooling. Its nested component format is not an obvious fit for Michi’s flat TOON list. | Compare representative golden outputs and escaping. Reuse Michi only where the format and truncation signals actually match; preserve Caliper’s canonical data contract. |
| **Callisto** | It already has a [versioned report envelope](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/output.rs:13>). Its [graph code](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/toposort.rs:29>) filters dependency kinds and uses SCCs to handle publish cycles. It does not currently depend on `michi-graph`. | Preserve report JSON. Explore an optional agent projection. Test graph behavior for parity before considering migration; the SCC and edge-filter rules make a replacement far from automatic. |
| **Firkin** | You confirmed implementation has not started. The [available research note](</Users/gabe/Projects/pages/docs/research/tools/firkin.md:1>) describes barrel generation but contains no technical output contract. | Design its canonical change report and agent projection together when the spec takes shape. Firkin is a prospective consumer, not evidence that a new Michi API is needed today. |

## What Michi already gets right

The external projects reinforce existing choices. [Starbase](https://docs.rs/crate/starbase/latest) keeps lifecycle outcomes explicit; Michi’s [pipeline records](</Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-pipeline/src/record.rs:228>) already retain step outcomes and identify work needing verification. Its [durable start hook](</Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-pipeline/src/exec.rs:72>) and resume tests cover the key replay concern. Cloudflare’s [Code Mode runtime](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/docs/codemode/runtime.md) likewise separates execution history from what is shown to a model. Michi should build on those boundaries, not add an agent loop or general event bus.

The most useful shared pattern is **canonical result first, bounded agent view second**. Caliper does this explicitly; Callisto’s reports provide a canonical result; Monokl has structured search results plus TOON projection. Cloudflare [Computer](https://github.com/cloudflare/computer/blob/main/docs/09_tool_interface.md) also keeps a tool library separate from framework adapters. That supports Michi’s current small core and separate pipeline crate.

## Proposed work, in order

1. **Correct the contract documents now.** State the MCP version Michi actually targets and update stale crate and release descriptions. The current [MCP adapter](</Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-core/src/mcp.rs:77>) requires object `structuredContent`, which is correct for [MCP 2025-11-25](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools). [MCP 2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools) permits any JSON value and shows `resultType` in results. Those are protocol changes requiring an explicit compatibility decision, not an incidental widening of one field.

2. **Run three consumer trials.** Migrate a small Monokl output path; compare Caliper golden fixtures against Michi rendering; and run Callisto graph parity cases covering dependency kinds, dev-only cycles, ordering, and diagnostics. Record where an adapter suffices and where Michi’s types truly fall short. Firkin can join once its output contract exists.

3. **Rework the proposed response envelope using those results.** [Michi’s `AgentResponse`](</Users/gabe/Projects/michi/crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:30>) currently renders one TOON or KV body. The [draft multi-section design](</Users/gabe/Projects/michi/docs/spec/07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md:1>) addresses a real shape limit, but its inclusion case remains open. Start with repeatable, named sections only if independent consumers need the *same* representation. Keep budget accounting, provenance, and indexed operation outcomes as separate decisions. Fix the draft’s `debug_assert!` plus release clamp: it conflicts with [PRINCIPLES.md](</Users/gabe/Projects/michi/PRINCIPLES.md:105>), which requires identical validation behavior in debug and release.

4. **Define an MCP version strategy before expanding the adapter.** Test serialized results against real clients for the chosen protocol version, including errors, audience annotations, text fallback, and structured content. Preserve domain-typed results in the consumer; Michi can map the agent view and wire envelope. Add a newer MCP profile only when a consumer needs it and compatibility tests establish its behavior.

5. **Publish integration examples after the trials.** A Monokl projection, a Caliper comparison, and a durable pipeline recipe would show how to use the existing crates. They should become adapters only if repeated consumer code justifies one.

I would **not** move Callisto’s release rules, Caliper’s type formatting, Monokl’s ranking, or Firkin’s file-generation policy into Michi. Each decides *what* happens; Michi’s reusable role is to render the result and communicate cuts, errors, and recovery clearly. That is also the inclusion test in [PRINCIPLES.md](</Users/gabe/Projects/michi/PRINCIPLES.md:9>).

This was a read-only assessment; I did not change files or run tests. The proposal’s main uncertainty is whether Caliper and Monokl require the same multi-section contract. The consumer trials are the decision gate for that API.
